name: gmp-ecm
desc: Elliptic Curve Method for integer factorization
why: Elliptic curve factoring is a real piece of number theory you can run at home on large integers.

brief.what_it_is: GMP-ECM is a command-line program called ecm that tries to factor large integers using the Elliptic Curve Method. The README I could reach was empty, so this is based on the Homebrew description and the GitLab project page. The Homebrew entry describes it as an Elliptic Curve Method tool for integer factorization. It takes an integer to factor and prints any factors it finds.
brief.why_it_exists: Not stated in the pages I could read. The Homebrew scout note frames it as a way to run real elliptic-curve number theory on large integers at home.
brief.install_notes: Installed through Homebrew as the formula gmp-ecm, which provides the executable ecm. The project page I fetched does not describe any setup beyond that. The name suggests a dependency on the GMP arbitrary-precision library, but I did not confirm that from the pages.
brief.standout: Elliptic curve factoring is a well-known algorithm for finding medium-sized prime factors of large numbers, and this is a long-established implementation of it. Running it on a laptop is a direct way to see the number theory at work.
brief.status: Unknown from what I could read. The GitLab project page shows it was created on October 09, 2020 and is licensed GNU GPLv3, but it shows no release date, last commit, or changelog contents. The README page loaded without any text.
brief.caveats: The GitLab README page loaded with no visible content, so I could not check usage, options, platform support, or build steps. The separate homepage I tried at members.loria.fr/PZimmermann/ecm returned HTTP 404. Anything beyond the licence, creation date, and Homebrew description is unverified.
